text: It was difficult to find info on this trail. So worth it. If you’re a proper hiker this is an easy trail. The locals will try and detour you so you take a taxi up. Happened to us, but thankfully we used it going down, walked from Big Buddha to the local town right to a health clinic. Easy. Great views on the tail too. Ropes for support, easy to navigate. Sad to see so much trash the whole way down.

I took the Big Buddha Hiking Trail and found it challenging but rewarding. The round trip from Karon Beach to Big Buddha and back was just under 90min, check opening hours first if you want to go in. I arrived at 7am and it opened at 9am - I was more interested in the challenge of the walk than visiting the Big Buddha. The trail itself was well signposted and required some dexterity to navigate, but was ok. It was a good workout on the trail and a little easier when hitting the road section up to the Big Buddha. Coming down was much quicker and aided by ropes in places. Even leaving early it was warm, so take plenty of water during the day. Disappointing to see some rubbish on the trail, please pick up after yourself.

It is NOT a casual stroll in the park, rather an all terrain assault course that really the SAS should use for training.

Beautiful views.

I am relatively fit but gave up half way up. Clint Eastwood said "A man's gotta know his limitations", so rather than risk a broken limb or heart attack my continuing overall trip around Asia was worth more to me than the treacherous (at times) climb.

I walked with walking shoes, but coming down saw people with sandals, crocks and flip flops..... insanity.

If you can do it, and want to take lots and lots of water and a towel. I took a change of shirt because the one worn going up was sodden with sweat.

Go luck to you if you attempt it, but please go prepared and take it gently and with care

I feel I need to share an honest review as some others on here are definitely a bit dramatic. So overall it’s a good little “trail”. Mostly walking up through the trees. If you’re lucky you’ll see some nature. From spiders to monkeys. Now this is where the negative reviews come in… the trail is and isn’t a trail. I get some may have this image of a nice mud path that goes up hill, which is the case for 1/2 of it. Other bits are a little sketchy perhaps but nothing that you can’t get around. There are some ropes to assist in areas. I’d suggest a decent shoe. But as I said, don’t go into this thinking it’s a stroll up a path. Fairly easy for someone who walks/ hikes a lot. Others may find it a little challenging. Roughly 20 minutes or so for the trail itself. Some cafes at the top of the trail, followed by a 10 - 15 minute walk to the Buddha.

It's not as easy as in some reviews. But if you enjoy the challenge, you will be rewarded.

The route consists of three parts.
1 - when you start in Kata. The road is good, but the angle of inclination is high. It's already difficult.
2 - in the jungle. Rocks, roots. The hardest part.
3 - the road is back. Nothing special. There are several cafes there. And you are next to the Buddha.

Some tips:
sportswear and shoes.
Take water if you plan to make stops. You start at 8:00 or 9:00 in the morning, while it's not so hot.
You can take a small towel (I was all wet).
One-way travel time is about 40 minutes.

Good luck

A VERY steep short trail, about 2,5km long, that gets you to the Buddha temple. It is very well paved and mostly with natural shadow. Great for a morning mini workout, definitely with shoes. There are some nice views along, a juice booth at 500m and lots of flora. 🌿🌱

Great workout. Nice adventure. The nature and the green all around is good. The slope is steep and highly recommend good shoes. There are parts with rope to help. There is wire cables hanging at the begging.
30 minutes to my pace. No monkeys.

Pretty difficult trail from Karon Beach up to the Big Buddha, so think twice before going-especially if it's raining. The path can get very slippery, and you might encounter monkeys or even snakes along the way.

That said, it's absolutely worth it. The hike is challenging but rewarding, and the views at the top are amazing. If you're into hiking and outdoor activities, this is a must-do in Phuket.

I also made a YouTube video about this trail, you can search by the name on YouTube: "The Hidden Jungle Trail to Big Buddha at Phuket"
It is steep but worth it. Last bit is paved road. There is a cafe with rabbits you can pet and they sell water. There are ropes to help your climb at the beginning. Take sunscreen and repellent.

The hiking trail is very challenging and steep, leading through dense jungle. In difficult sections, there are ropes to help you climb. Along the way, you might encounter plenty of insects and reptiles, such as spiders or frogs. Your shoes will definitely get muddy! The worst part is the big electric cables hanging at shoulder height — you really need to watch out for those. Overall, I really enjoyed it! It was a great experience and I totally recommend it.
A wonderful hiking trail that ends with a visit to the temple. We love this location with all our hearts; it's our tradition to visit it when we arrive in Phuket.

Very nice trail for a walk, you might run into a few monkeys, as well as some stunning Russian women. None of them are aggressive, but be warned: a few might try to recruit you for “work” and relieve you of your assets
Short trail but very steep. Advised to wear sport shoes. There is a very nice juice bar just at the beginning of the trail.
Short but challenging hike, more so in the high sun. Sounds of forest, great views and Buddha atmosphere is marvellous.
Path is very steep, but it'll get you there. Bring enough water especially if you're going mid day. On the top there's bars, shop and a restaurant. Wouldn't recommend during the rainy season

Lovely steep short “hike” to the big Buddha. Most of the time is more like a climb. It rained a lot during my climb so a lot of mud. At some points there are ropes to help you, but overal can be quite challenging. I loved the closeness to the jungle and the viewpoints.

A lovely and challenging hiking trail with a steep incline. Terrain is slippery even when it is dry, especially while walking downhill.

Bring water, closed shoes, and mosquito spray. It will get very hot.

Hard to rate this trail… overall 5 stars. Not for the average hiker, challenging in some spots and can get slippery from loose dirt or mud. Plan on amazing views and getting sweaty. Worth the hike but easy to drive up if you’re in a hurry. Keep in mind the Big Buddha is a religious temple, so it is respectful to wear appropriate garments(some options are provided for sale or rent)

The trail itself isn't too long but it' steep in some areas with some rope that can be used.I actually saw some people working on the very beginning of the trail.

It took me about 30 minutes to get to the top of the trail and another 10 minutes all the way to Big Bhudda. I did the ascent in the middle of the day and it got quite hot, so be prepared and bring some water.
Did the descend just before sunset and that was a bit easier and quite a bit faster. Its slippery though.

Like other people mentioned, use decent shoes. Also there are some electrical wires which you should probably avoid.

All in all, nice little adventure.

Went early morning in dry season. From Kata beach we got a taxi to the trailhead and then walked back to town after. Not as tough as I expected based on reviews. A few mosquitoes, a few monkeys, amazing views at the top and can still get half decent look at Buddha even though it’s currently closed! Well worth it! Recommend plenty of water and proper shoes and moderate level of fitness. It is a bit slippy coming down so take it slow.
This trail made the Big Buddha visit memorable. If you are atleast a little bit fit then you can make it even in Birkenstocks, lol.

From the actual start of the trail up to the tarmac road that leads to the Budha, it should take most people 30 to 50 mins, depending on fitness, time of day, weather and personal kit. Then another 10mins or so along the road at the top …

Kata hiking trail to big Buddha
This trail became really popular back the at the beginning of Covid when they closed all the beaches and people still wanted to get out and do some exercise. Theres been a lot of modifications to the trail since then, making it a bit safer for everyone to use. The trail from the beginning to the big buddha road is about 20 minutes non stop walking or 30-40 minutes with a few breaks and another 10-15 minutes to reach the big buddha statue. The trail through the jungle is actually only about 1km, it just has a been incline the whole way up. The best time to go is in the morning or late afternoon, as its generally a bit cooler than. Once you reach the road theres a few sea view cafes which is definitely a great place to catch your breath and indulge in a fresh cold coconut. The best time to spot the monkeys is late afternoon around 4-5pm, just be careful to not get to close as these are wild monkeys, If you do come across them on the route, just keep walking and view from a safe distance.
I walk up here quite regularly with my dog and he loves the trail, great way to tire him out haha.
What to bring?
Bring closed in footwear as the trail can be slippy with quite a few loose rocks.
Mosquito spray is needed in the wetter months, as you get a lot once you enter the jungle.
Bring some water to keep refreshed.
You cannot drive this trail on a motorbike... i have seen people try , your bike will get stuck.
Doing the climb with young kids is possible, I would highly recommend not doing it with a pushchair though, as you will need free hands to be able to climb up.
Enjoy the trek!

A decent walk with a few challenging areas, but should be accessible to most people. There are ropes in the more steeper areas to help when walking up and down. You will need actual shoes for the walk but trainers will be fine. We didn’t rush our way up and it took us 40 minutes to complete the trail, and a further 10 minutes to walk to the Big Buddha. Others have mentioned seeings snakes and other animals whilst walking, luckily we didn’t see any! Make sure you bring water too, you’ll need it no matter the time of day

The hike itself was alright. At the end of May, the weather will not be favorable. When we reached halfway, the road was blocked maybe due to the weather. Steep incline but we were wearing sandals and it was still manageable.

It’s fun!😅we accidentally ended up hiking that trail up to the big Buddha, but it made the view up there even more fun, since you’ve put a lot of effort into getting up there 😅it’s a nice hike. It will take you about 40 minutes trough the …

Ok! So this hike is not 20mins long. It is about an hour hike and it is tough to say the least.
Coming from two fit 30 year olds, we found this extremely challenging in the heat of the day. Take sunscreen, water and insect repellent. Remember to wear long pants and cover your shoulders when visiting the Buddha.

Nice and steep, ropes were available in the steepest sections. A lot of rain erosion on the dirt sections of the trail.  Closer to the top, you walk through a paved Road between a rubber tree plantation. If you're coming from Karon or Katang Beach, you can hike up about as quickly as a drive to the top of the Big Buddha because the roads take you all the way to the east side of the island before wrapping back around.  If you're coming from the Western beaches, this hiking trail goes straight up the hill and right to the Big Buddha.  It took my wife and I 45 minutes to hike up the trail, and it took us 45 minutes in a cab to get back!
The hike is hard but not too long only 1km but very steep terrain, not recommended in heavy rain.

I took abt 60 min to finish the trail from the starting point to the Big Buddha. Not too hard, not too easy. But I think it is a bit dangerous in rainy season because it is quite slippery and there are electrical wires along the way.
Super and there are not so many people!

We were descending after visiting the Big Buddha. The trail was wet and a little scary, but we made it. We had an umbrella, SPF, and trekking sandals. The point wasn't open, and we encountered a large family of monkeys along the way (it's a shame there were no treats), as well as lizards, butterflies, and cicadas.
great
This is a great way to get to the Big Buddha statue while getting some exercise; the route is just over 1 km. I recommend going when the weather is dry and wearing closed-toe shoes.

Off into the wilderness!

Important: A basic level of fitness is required, as the ascent is extremely steep in places, especially in hot weather. So, wear sturdy shoes (suitable for uneven terrain), bring plenty of water, a hat, and sunscreen. There's a small stand where you can buy drinks about halfway along the route.

The trail leads over asphalt, a mix of sand and stones, and a forest path completely covered in roots.
Great place to visit while in Phuket

A decent trail to the Big Buddha. Overall, the trail is fairly easy, about 30 minutes to the Buddha, and even easier to get back. Unfortunately, I didn't see any monkeys along the way, even though I went just to see them, but it was still interesting to walk along the trail.
Tough trail with parts that feel more like climbing, worth it!
Beautiful panoramic views of Phuket
Serene experience; felt deeply peaceful looking at the big 45-meter marble statue of Lord Buddha.
A gorgeous trail. Sneakers are a must. Magnificent views along the way. I highly recommend this route to the Big Buddha.
It's quite challenging if you're unprepared; the sweat and fat will run into your sneakers! We walked for 1.5-2 hours, including rest stops. Be sure to bring water and sports shoes!

This is a difficult climb, which consists of a continuous up hill climb with no real flat areas until you reach the top. It took me approximately 1 hour from kata town to the top, I used google maps and it took me through the forest.

Lots of uneven ground, although there is ropes in places it still is difficult.

I would consider myself to have a good level of fitness and I did have to stop a few times. I met many people who were struggling, or even had turned around.

If your in to hiking and like a challenge, then definitely give this a go. I stupidly climbed with no water, massive mistake! Once you get back onto the road there is restaurants/ cafes where you can get a drink and enjoy a view over kata / karon beach.

The buddah was free entry but be sure to cover your knees and shoulders.

There was lots of monkeys at the top during my visit!
It was a great trip. The way back wasn't easy, though. It rained very heavily. But no matter. All in all, it was a fantastic experience.
The path to the Big Buddha is only accessible from 9:00 AM onwards.
A fantastic experience! We booked it through Get Your Guide and were taken directly there.
Great view, entrance fee 100 baht, because I was with a girl and had to buy a cape for 200 baht, but they gave me 100 back on the way out. Look for monkeys in the trees.

What a twist 😅🤣
There's no Buddha here, just a path leading to it!
We're back! It's better to take a taxi there; you'll get there in 8 minutes, rather than walking for an hour and feeling half-dead 🫠

Not for the weak or frail! Good hike with an easy to follow path, mostly sheltered but the heat and humidity will still get you
There is one store at the start of the trail proper but it was empty for me till I got to the road section

I hiked from a beachfront hotel to the Buddha from 11:00 AM to 11:55 AM, having looked at the route on maps and YouTube beforehand. Sneakers and water are essential. About 800 meters up a very narrow, difficult path with a rope for assistance. At this pace, the climb is quite strenuous. On the way back, I was surprised to encounter an elderly couple of unathletic-looking people in flip-flops. I talked them out of it, saying they could break their feet in those shoes, and their shoes wouldn't hold up anyway.
The reviews are quite varied, and it's difficult to get a clear picture of the climb's difficulty level if you rely solely on the opinions of gym-goers. …
With heat: 40 degrees, we couldnt do more than 300 meters. Too hard to hike  for beginners
A relaxed after-work get-together
A wonderful place, you should definitely visit it.
It was difficult to climb, but the main thing is that there is a path.
A fairly challenging trail offering an alternative to the long road to reach the Big Buddha area. Several beautiful viewpoints along the way. The trailhead is not always known to taxi drivers/Grabs.

This is not a trail for those who are not used to it. Don't go in thinking it's just a walk and that's it.
The climb is steep and it gets very stuffy because of the heat. In some …

It was quite an adventure! At times we were almost at our wits' end, but in the end we were proud and happy! We were a three-generation group (between 23 and 71 years old) and underestimated the hiking trail. The heat, steep sections, and climbing were really tough for my parents, but they made it! "Grandma, the body can handle more than you think!"

When we reached the Buddha, we were happy and thrilled!

Be sure to wear good shoes and bring plenty of water!
A very easy hiking trail if you go to the gym every day, wear hiking boots, bring an oxygen tent, and three liters of water. …
However, it's a bit more challenging than expected. Anyone who isn't very fit shouldn't attempt it.

There were mixed reviews on the difficulty of this trail. So we took the gamble and went as it was right by our Airbnb. We went at high sun because we wanted a "slow day" and got up late. Mistake #1, no slow days in Thailand get up with the sun it's too damn hot. We thought 600ml each of water would be enough, mistake #2. We wore long clothing to protect from bugs, mistakish #3, you will be completely soaked by the time you get up, use bug spray and you will be fine. There were times I wanted to die. I begged my husband to leave my body for the scorpions.  I fell a few times on the way back down but I am quiet clumsy. It is steep, there are ropes, use them up and down. As fit-ish late 20s year olds we had a hard time going up. There is a restaurant at the top called big Buddha art cafe. Absolutely delicious. There was trash everywhere, please respect Thailand and pack out your trash ☺️
Free, if you want to sweat and really let off steam, beautiful climb, only 30 minutes uphill in the jungle.
A nice little hike up to Big Buddha, make sure you wear decent shoes
